text: For most job-based and individual health plans, you get at least 180 days after receiving a denial to file an internal appeal.
HealthCare.gov says an internal appeal must be decided within 30 days for care you haven’t received yet, and within 60 days for care you already received.
Under federal claims rules for employer plans, an urgent care claim must be decided as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the plan receives it.
After a final internal denial, you generally have 4 months to request an independent external review.
HealthCare.gov says your insurer is required by law to accept the external reviewer’s decision.
New Jersey’s Independent Health Care Appeals Program (IHCAP) does not accept appeals for self-funded plans, Medicare, Medicare Advantage, or insurance contracts delivered in another state.
IHCAP generally requires you to finish the plan’s internal appeal first.
NJ DOBI says a standard IHCAP decision takes no more than 45 calendar days from when the appeal is submitted.
NJ DOBI lists 1-888-393-1062 or 609-777-9470 for questions about the Independent Health Care Appeals Program.
For problems with a New Jersey-regulated insurer, NJ DOBI’s Consumer Hotline is 1-800-446-7467.
Federal claims rules for job-based plans generally apply to private-sector employer plans, with exceptions for plans sponsored by government or most religious bodies.
The U.S. Department of Labor says you have at least 180 days to appeal a denied claim under a private employer plan.

Job-based plans that aren’t grandfathered must provide external review of claim denials by an independent party. Plans set up after March 23, 2010, or that made certain significant changes after that date, are not grandfathered.
In Medicaid managed care, you generally have 60 calendar days from the date on the notice to appeal to the plan.

After the plan’s appeal decision, federal rules give at least 90 and at most 120 days to request a State fair hearing. New Jersey changed parts of its fair hearing process in 2026, so follow the deadline printed on your notice.
If you’re in a Medicare Advantage or other Medicare plan, the plan must tell you in writing how to appeal. Medicare generally has 5 levels of appeal.
In a Medicare Advantage plan, a request for reconsideration generally must be filed within 60 calendar days after you receive the plan’s written decision.

Under CMS’s prior authorization rule (CMS-0057-F), Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid programs, and plans on the federal marketplace must give a specific reason when they deny a prior authorization request (drug requests excluded). That reason goes to your provider, so ask them for it.
